scope.purpose: Verify four additional CV publications and distinguish historical and current FlowPilot case-study references; record a limited chemistry and citation audit.
scope.cv_access: Read locally with pdftotext; the file was present during this research.
scope.publication_verification_policy: Use primary publisher records for publication metadata and supported literature claims; use the CV only to establish CV membership. Local manuscript and collaborator records are separately attributed.
scope.access_limitations: Some direct publisher requests returned HTTP 403. Publisher-indexed article text and publisher issue or author records were also used. Metadata verification does not imply that every full article or supporting-information file was read.
scope.placement_recommendations: Editorial recommendations based on the round-2 manuscript extraction, not instructions contained in the cited publications.
scope.duplicate_check: All four new CV reference DOIs and titles were absent from both reviewed manuscript reference lists.

case_study_references.title: α‑Bromination of Aldehydes by Continuous Flow Chemistry and Its Application to the Flow Synthesis of 2‑Aminothiazoles

primary_sources.supports: Complete author list, published title, DOI, dates and abstract.
Volume 29, issue 8, pages 2047-2055 and publication dates.

case_study_references.supported_claim: Aldehydes undergo continuous-flow alpha-bromination with bromine, with improved efficiency and mono/dibromination selectivity compared with batch; the approach is extended to multistep 2-aminothiazole synthesis.

local_preprint_evidence.description: Reference 43 matches this publication. The historical case describes 3-phenylpropanal/Br2 in MeCN followed by sodium thiosulfate quench.

case_study_references.verification_boundary: The full citation and abstract-level chemistry are publisher-verified. The particular inline quench, two-reactor topology, substrate-specific conditions and numerical comparisons in the preprint were not independently checked against the publisher's supporting information in this audit.
case_study_references.current_manuscript_disposition: Retain only for historical provenance or an explicitly labeled historical comparison; do not use as the current Figure 6 DPDTC reference.

case_study_references.role: Current round-2 Figure 6 and reference 43: telescoped DPDTC-mediated amidation
case_study_references.title: Flow-to-Flow Technology: Amide Formation in the Absence of Traditional Coupling Reagents Using DPDTC

primary_sources.supports: Complete author list, title, journal, year, volume, issue, pages, DOI, dates and thioester-to-amide chemistry.

case_study_references.supported_claim: DPDTC activates carboxylic acids to thioesters in flow; subsequent reaction with amines produces amides without requiring intermediate isolation.
case_study_references.claim_boundary: DPDTC is itself a coupling reagent. The title does not imply reagent-free amidation. Literature outcomes do not establish the performance of FlowPilot's proposed apparatus or conditions.

local_manuscript_evidence.description: The current case and Figure 6 caption explicitly concern DPDTC-mediated amidation through a thioester intermediate, with prospective laboratory results.

case_study_references.role: Figure 5 source and primary record for liquid backflow into the gas line
case_study_references.title: Batch and flow synthesis of sulfides and sulfoxides using green solvents and oxidant through visible-light photocatalysis

primary_sources.supports: Complete author list, title, journal, year, volume, pages and DOI.
Results and discussion around Table 4: direction of backflow, oxygen flow settings, BPR settings, and distinction between batch air exposure and flow oxygen feed.

case_study_references.supported_claim: Photoredox C-C bond formation produces a sulfide that is subsequently photooxidized to a sulfoxide.

literature_backflow_event.location: Results and discussion, Table 4 entry 3 and accompanying paragraph
literature_backflow_event.direction: LIQUID reaction solution into GAS line
literature_backflow_event.pressure_basis: Not independently resolved as gauge or absolute in this audit; preserve the publisher's bar label.
literature_backflow_event.gas_flow_reference_conditions: Not established in this audit; do not silently relabel the published set flow as STP flow.
literature_backflow_event.interpretation_limit: These settings describe one apparatus, not a universal backflow threshold or a remedy for gas intrusion into an upstream liquid reactor.

chemistry_pitfall_audit.finding: Do not conflate the literature's liquid-into-gas-line event with the collaborator's gas-into-Stage-1 event.

collaborator_event.direction: GAS entering upstream Stage 1 through the connected liquid-side path
collaborator_event.provenance: User's explicit report in this conversation, 2026-09-22
collaborator_event.verification_status: Reported observation; original collaborator correspondence and raw pressure traces were not inspected in this audit

chemistry_pitfall_audit.recommendation: Attribute each observation separately, state its direction, and do not transfer the literature's low-flow explanation or numerical settings to the collaborator event. A connectivity finding alone does not establish a pressure-transient cause.

chemistry_pitfall_audit.finding: The Giese paper uses air exposure in batch but an oxygen feed in its flow optimization. Neither lower inlet gas volume nor a gas-branch check valve establishes protection of the upstream liquid branch.
chemistry_pitfall_audit.evidence_type: Publisher gas-identity distinction plus locally documented engineering scope limits
chemistry_pitfall_audit.recommendation: Preserve gas identity and oxygen molar feed in comparisons. Treat air-to-oxygen substitution as an unvalidated proposal requiring oxygen-service review; it does not remove an unprotected reverse path.

chemistry_pitfall_audit.finding: The historical preprint and current round-2 manuscript both use reference number 43 and Figure 6 for different chemistry.
chemistry_pitfall_audit.evidence_type: Direct comparison of local manuscript extractions
chemistry_pitfall_audit.recommendation: Match sources by DOI and manuscript version, not figure or reference number alone. Do not carry bromination captions, thiosulfate quench operations, conditions or validation claims into the DPDTC case.

chemistry_pitfall_audit.finding: The supplied DPDTC sequence has activation followed by benzylamine addition. Its stated post-addition concentration is not automatically the concentration of a separate amine feed.
chemistry_pitfall_audit.evidence_type: Local protocol review and arithmetic; not a new experimental observation
chemistry_pitfall_audit.calculation: The initial acid charge is 0.5 mmol in 1.0 mL (0.5 M). Adding 0.25 mL solvent gives a nominal acid-derived concentration of 0.5 mmol / 1.25 mL = 0.4 M, neglecting reagent volumes. This does not specify the amine stock concentration for a pumped flow feed.
chemistry_pitfall_audit.recommendation: Maintain activation-before-amine staging, recompute downstream flow after interstage addition, and separately specify each feed's concentration and molar flow. Do not describe DPDTC amidation as coupling-reagent-free.

chemistry_pitfall_audit.finding: Inlet/STP apparent space time is not measured in-channel gas-liquid residence time, and numerical closure is not experimental validation.
chemistry_pitfall_audit.evidence_type: Scope limits already stated in the current manuscript and local operability review
chemistry_pitfall_audit.recommendation: Retain the declared flow reference conditions and pressure basis. Do not infer conversion, yield, a successful backflow remedy, or laboratory approval from recalculated time or inventory closure. Keep Figures 5 and 6 prospective until actual outcomes are supplied.
